title: Superior level cut six-month Michigan-Huron forecast error by 5.54% after twelve local monthly changes at 1970-2024 issues
abstract: We tested whether a year of local monthly level changes removes added information from Lake Superior in six-month Michigan-Huron forecasts. We used coordinated v2025 levels and 660 issue months in 1970-2024. Adding Superior level reduced mean squared error by 5.54%. The conditional 95% five-year block interval was 0.74% to 9.62%. RMSE fell from 0.14459 to 0.14053 m. The reverse forecast had a point loss. The directional gain difference was 8.96 percentage points, with an interval of 2.28 to 15.70. The gain persisted with 3, 6 and 24 local monthly changes. A rolling forty-year fit gave an interval that included zero. The richer own-lake model did not improve on the simpler own-lake benchmark. This is a test of added information in linear models, not a test of physical transport or operational skill. Revised data, uneven skill over time, conditional intervals and omitted weather and regulation limit the result. The package includes original code, exact source provenance, aggregate evidence, bootstrap scores and a figure. Source records and individual predictions are retrieved or regenerated outside the signed draft.

display.caption: Added other-lake information after local history adjustment at 660 six-month forecast issues. Error bars use paired five-year blocks and condition on the fitted forecasts. MH means Michigan-Huron; S means Superior. The rolling-history intervals include zero. Cumulative curves sum annual mean squared-error reductions and do not measure water transport.
